clue.text: Really hate Dutch quiz European puts on

indicators.note: in an across answer the E is put on, ahead of, the quiz word

parts.note: a quiz is a test

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a Dutch quiz that a European has staged.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something intensely is exactly what it means to abhor or truly despise it.

clue.text: Beastly sort of racket's got to finish early

parts.note: a din is a racket, a loud noise

indicators.note: the word stops early, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nasty kind of tennis racket has to be put away before the match ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild dog of Australia is a kind of beast, hence a beastly sort.

clue.text: Fish seen about river briefly in the country

indicators.note: the fish sits about, around, the shortened river

parts.note: a tuna is a fish

indicators.note: briefly cuts the last letter from the river word

parts.note: the Isis is the name of the Thames at Oxford

explanation.surface: Fish are spotted around a river for a short while somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African nation on the Mediterranean coast, hence a country.

clue.text: Small, flapping beasts on large perch

indicators.note: flapping means in a flap, agitated, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Little birds flap about on a big branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like a bird's roost but is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreckfish, a big sea fish of the perch-like order, is a kind of large perch.

clue.text: Make of old aircraft with the letter E in it

indicators.note: having something in it says the given letter sits inside the aircraft word

parts.note: crate is slang for an old, rickety aeroplane
spelled out plainly as the single letter

explanation.surface: A model maker builds a replica of a vintage plane bearing the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for bringing something into being, a straightforward synonym pair.

clue.text: Locomotives won't start in downpours

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: trains are locomotives

explanation.surface: Engines refuse to start up in heavy storms.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy showers of falling water from the sky, in the plural noun sense.

clue.text: A vicar gets upset with Times being mean

indicators.note: upset turns the word over, reading it backwards in a down answer

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
an age is a period of time, so times

explanation.surface: A clergyman is upset by the newspaper being unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper and 'mean' like nasty; they are ages and the arithmetic mean.
explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic mean is the typical value, the sum divided by the count.

clue.text: Those making trunk calls plan these changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Telephone users making long-distance calls review their tariff changes.
explanation.walkthrough: A trunk call is an old British term for a long-distance phone call; here the trunk is a pachyderm's nose.
explanation.definitionFit: These pachyderms trumpet through their trunks, so they make calls with them.

clue.text: Continually working? A fellow must grab bit of nap!

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: the fellow phrase grabs, holding the next letter inside it

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: a bit of nap is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone always at work: a college fellow must snatch a quick nap!
explanation.walkthrough: 'must grab' puts N inside A DON, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something happening without stopping, over and over for a long time.

clue.text: A stiff drink sent flying in revel

indicators.note: the letters are scattered, as if knocked over, and land in a new order

explanation.surface: At a party, someone's strong cocktail gets knocked over by the revellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick-me-up drink, especially alcohol taken to perk oneself up, is called by this informal name.

clue.text: Architect's firm finally prosper with more work on

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of prosper

parts.note: having more work on means being busier

explanation.surface: A design practice finally thrives as it takes on more commissions.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Corbusier was the Swiss-French modernist building designer.

clue.text: I boot users out for this sort of behaviour

definitions.text: I boot users out for this sort of behaviour

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bouncer or forum moderator explains why rowdy members get ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rowdy, noisy conduct is exactly why someone is booted out.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy, rowdy and unruly conduct is the kind that gets people thrown out of a place.

clue.text: Long piece of asparagus given to short cook

indicators.note: a piece of asparagus is its first letter
short means the cook word loses its last letter

parts.note: a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: A tall spear of asparagus is served to a cook of little stature.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn or pine for it, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Animal some sell: a marsupial?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pet shop advertisement: some sell a kangaroo-like creature, or so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American camelid, the woolly pack beast of the Andes, is one example of a creature.

clue.text: Crushed parsley on ham?

indicators.note: crushed means mangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe query: chopped herbs sprinkled over cured pork?
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the meat but means an amateur, as in a ham radio operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an amateur, a non-professional, which is the sense of a non-expert.

clue.text: Resentful son steals new waders

indicators.note: the phrase steals the letter, taking it inside

parts.note: bitter means resentful

explanation.surface: A grudging son pinches some new fishing waders.
explanation.definitionFit: These are marsh birds of the heron family, and wading birds are commonly called waders.

clue.text: Look critically at what a shoplifter is apt to do?

definitions.meaning: to review a situation and assess it carefully

definitions.text: what a shoplifter is apt to do?
definitions.meaning: literally, to steal merchandise from a shop

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to assess a situation, while a shoplifter literally lifts goods held by a store.

clue.text: Ways for one to easily get round cities?

definitions.text: Ways for one to easily get round cities?

parts.words: Ways for one to easily get round cities?
parts.note: sounds like public transport around town, but means ring roads that let drivers skirt a city altogether

explanation.walkthrough: 'get round' suggests moving about inside a city; the roads meant go around it instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring roads built to route traffic around a town centre rather than through it.

clue.text: Organise a series of summits around October's end

indicators.note: the a-plus-peaks phrase goes around that letter

parts.note: a mountain range is a series of peaks

indicators.note: the end of October is its final letter

explanation.surface: Plan a mountain trek for late October.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in order or plan them is a direct synonym of organise.

clue.text: Dine in empty KFCs? That's romantic!

indicators.note: the dining word goes in the emptied shop name
an empty word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A wry take on dinner dates in deserted fried chicken shops.
explanation.walkthrough: KFCs emptied is KS. 'Romantic' is capitalised in sense: the poet was one of the Romantic movement.
explanation.definitionFit: John the poet was a leading figure of the English Romantic movement, so he is a Romantic.

clue.text: Italian peer supporting a conservative bill

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece goes beneath the others

parts.note: a conte, a count, is an Italian nobleman

explanation.surface: An Italian nobleman backs a right-wing politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of money owed, such as an invoice, is an account.

clue.text: Sport is combat without extermination primarily

indicators.note: without here means outside, so combat wraps round the letter

parts.note: war is combat

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of extermination

explanation.surface: A pacifist's slogan: sport is fighting minus the killing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport a garment or badge is to have it on, display it on oneself.

clue.text: Fabric wise chap's brought to foolish sort

parts.note: a seer is a wise prophet
a sucker is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A sage's material is passed to a gullible fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A puckered striped cotton cloth, often used for summer suits.

clue.text: Feel uptight? Time to leave for northern tip of Sardinia!

indicators.note: the time letter leaves and the next letter takes its place

parts.note: tense means uptight

indicators.note: in a down answer the northern tip is the first letter

explanation.surface: Feeling stressed? Time to set off for the north of Sardinia!
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to perceive or detect something is to feel it.

clue.text: Want to sack foremost of divas in The Globe

indicators.note: sack means dismiss, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a dearth is a want, a lack

indicators.note: foremost of picks the first letter of divas

explanation.surface: A wish to fire leading ladies at the Globe Theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Globe' suggests Shakespeare's London theatre; it means our planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet is often called the globe, the world we live on.

clue.text: A transgression that's consuming knight is silly

parts.note: a sin is a transgression

indicators.note: the i.e. letters consume, swallowing the knight letter

parts.note: i.e. stands for 'that is'
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A wrong that swallows up a knight is foolish behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' gives IE (id est, 'that is'), which wraps N.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something extremely foolish or stupid, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sadly rue orgy and mischievous acts

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters going wrong and being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a wild party and the naughty things done there.
explanation.definitionFit: Knavish or playfully naughty conduct, the behaviour of a rascal.

clue.text: Pleasant son welcomes English relatives

indicators.note: the pleasant-son pair welcomes the letter inside

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A kind son extends a welcome to visiting English family members.
explanation.definitionFit: Daughters of one's brother or sister are family members, so kin or relatives.

clue.text: A perfunctory design of small sailing vessel

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A quick plan drawn up for a little yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, quickly made drawing or outline is exactly a hasty, perfunctory plan.
